rationale: While indie hackers running multi-product portfolios do experience the friction of juggling separate dashboards, the evidence base is thin: the single source is a low-engagement dev.to post (score 22, 3 comments), and no direct willingness-to-pay signals—competitor pricing pages, paid job ads, or prospect quotes—have been located. The pain is real but diffuse and mild; most operators tolerate it with lightweight spreadsheets or simply don't prioritize unified analytics at the $500–5k MRR stage. The segment is also global-but-shallow (relatively few people run 3–30 products simultaneously at meaningful revenue), making TAM difficult to defend above $2–3M globally. Insufficient evidence to pass the 5-distinct-pain-quotes and ≥1 WTP signal threshold; recommend re-queuing after a broader scrape of IndieHackers, HN 'Ask HN: how do you manage multiple SaaS products', and Twitter/X threads.
